events.name: The Warning
events.intro:
A village is throwing stones at an Absol on the ridge. It does not leave.

**Goody Prowse:** "It came before the flood. It came before the fire. Drive it off and we'll pay."

*A stone hits it. It does not flinch. It looks at the school.*

success.text: You step up with your team, and the stones stop, because now somebody else is doing it. The Absol looks at you. It looks at you for a long time. It does not look afraid. It looks sorry.

choices.label: Stand between it and the stones.

success.text:
You step between. A stone hits your bag, and then another, and then the throwing stops, one arm at a time.

Goody Prowse lowers hers last. The Absol looks at you once. Then it turns and walks up the ridge, and stops, and waits.

The Absol goes up the ridge without looking back. You follow it, and the village watches you go.

Above the school there is a crack in the hillside. It is wet. It is widening. Nobody else has looked up here in a week.

events.name: The Slide
events.intro:
The crack goes. A sound like a door in the sky, and then the hill starts moving, all of it, quietly.

The Absol is already at the school, and so are you. It is the only warning anyone is going to get, and you have six turns.

*Every task is a person.*

success.text: Anything strong or large takes a child under each arm and runs. They are heavy, and wet, and silent. You count heads. The count is right. You count again.

choices.label: Dig a channel to turn the slide.

success.text: Claws, fists and shoulders cut a trench across the slope, as deep as they can make it, as fast as they can make it. The mud arrives at it, and leans, and starts to go the other way.

branches.text: A sound move, as loud as you can make it. It rolls down the street and into every house, and every house wakes up at once. Somebody laughs, crying, in the dark.

success.text: Every window on the street lights up. Doors bang. Nobody remembers dressing, and everybody is dressed.

branches.text: Steel takes the door and does not bend. The mud hits it, and it holds, and it holds, and the last child is out.

success.text: Something brave puts its shoulder to the school door and does not give. Behind it, small hands pass children out through the gap, one at a time.

events.name: The Slide, Turn 2
events.intro:
Turn 2 of 6. The crack above the school has widened to a hand. Mud runs down it, brown and slow, and then not so slow.

Voices below. A bell, rung wrong. Somebody is carrying a child on their back and does not know which way to go.

events.name: The Slide, at Night
events.intro:
That night, the hill comes down.

The Absol is already there, digging at the school door with its horn. It did not wait to be asked, and it did not wait to be forgiven.

There are three turns. Somebody has to be quicker than the mud.

events.name: The Slide: The Count
events.intro:
The hill stops. It takes a long time to be sure that it has stopped.

Everybody is in the square, in the rain, in whatever they were wearing. Nobody is missing. Goody Prowse counts heads, and gets the right number, and counts again.

*Nobody died. Buildings did.*

success.text: The old cart shed at the foot of the ridge is gone. It was always going to go. It was in the way of a hill.

effects.text: The school is standing. The channel you dug took the mud round it, and laid it down in the bottom field, a foot from the wall.
The school is gone. Nothing turned the slide, and it went through the classroom wall and out the other side. The children were already out of it.
The houses on the low street were awake in time: their doors were braced and their shutters barred, and they stand, with mud to the sills.
The houses on the low street are gone. Nobody woke them early; the families got out by the back windows, at the last, with nothing in their hands.
The school porch held, because something held its door. The bell is still hanging in it.
The school porch is gone, door and bell and all. Nobody held it. The last children came out through a window.
The little ones were carried out first, so there were hands to spare, and the hands saved the bakery: its wall was propped before the mud reached it.
The bakery is gone. The little ones walked out on their own feet, slowly, and every spare hand in the village was holding one of theirs.

events.name: After the Slide
events.intro:
It is quiet after. Mud to the windowsills. Nobody is under it.

Goody Prowse is sitting in the street with a child on her knee, counting heads. She counts them twice.

The Absol stands on the ridge, in the grey light, looking at the village.

success.text:
It does not run. It looks like something that was right, and is too tired to be glad of it.

Nobody says the word sorry out loud. The village sends up a pot of something warm, which is how a village says it.

effects.text: An Absol warned a village about the slide. It was believed too late by some, and in time by enough.

success.text:
It does not run. It looks at your hands, and the hands of everyone behind you, and every one of them has held a stone.

It turns and walks over the ridge, and does not look back. You do not follow. Some things are not yours to ask for.

effects.text: The village drove the Absol off, and it came back to dig anyway. Nobody has forgotten it.

events.name: Before the Fall
events.intro:
It comes down off the ridge slowly, as if the ground might change its mind.

It stops an arm's length away. Then it presses its forehead to the back of your hand and stays there.

It knows what comes before the falling. It will tell you, every time.

success.text: It falls in beside you. Somewhere behind, a child is waving from the school steps.

events.name: The Pile of Stones
events.intro:
A small shrine at the edge of a road, with a flat stone for an offering and a dish of water in front of it.

Behind it, on the ridge, there are stones. They are stacked in a neat pile, each one set on the last.

Somebody stacked them. Nobody threw them.

choices.label: Leave a stone on the pile.

success.text: You set it on top, gently, the way you would put down something that could still hurt. The wind turns, and for a moment the whole ridge sounds like someone saying thank you.
You walk on. Behind you, the pile does not move. It is not going to.
